tagline: The first federal highway, Baltimore to the Mississippi.
intro: Out of Baltimore the old pike heads west to Cumberland and over the Allegheny Mountains, past the toll gate house at La Vale and across the Casselman River near Grantsville. In Pennsylvania it passes the Summit Inn and Fort Necessity and comes down to the Monongahela at Brownsville. It crosses the Ohio at Wheeling, and from there it is US 40 through the pike towns of Ohio and Indiana, through Columbus and Indianapolis, across Illinois to East St. Louis.

Congress authorized the road in 1806 and it reached Wheeling in 1818. Federal crews got as far as Vandalia by 1839. In 1840 Congress voted against finishing it, Henry Clay casting the deciding vote. The railroads were coming.

moments.title: Casselman Bridge
moments.text: An 80-foot stone arch of 1813, the largest in America at the time, that carried 12-horse teams hauling 10-ton loads and has been closed to vehicles since 1953.

moments.title: Wheeling Suspension Bridge
moments.text: Charles Ellet's span over the Ohio was the largest suspension bridge in the world in 1849, lost its deck to a windstorm in 1854, and has been closed to cars since 2019.

moments.title: Vandalia State House
moments.text: Illinois put up this brick statehouse in 1836, and the next February the legislature, pressed by a caucus led by young Abraham Lincoln, voted to move the capital to Springfield.
